benchmark: VERITAS Table I, rows P8-P10 (out-of-bounds vulnerabilities only)
source_paper: Veritas: Grounding LLM Agents for Reliable Vulnerability Reasoning over Stripped Binaries, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15097
compile_protocol: -O0; unstripped binary for ground-truth mapping, stripped copy for binary-level audit, ASan build for PoC reproduction (see benchmark/build.sh).

validation.method: CVE records + SourceForge bug tracker cross-referenced; both functions located in ezxml.c at this exact commit. lxfontes/ezxml mirrors ezXML 0.8.6 and dcb1748 is its last (unpatched) commit, so the 2021 CVEs against 0.8.6 apply directly.

vulnerabilities.sink_description: While parsing a crafted internal DTD, a one-byte constant (';') is written past the end of the buffer: `*(s = n + strcspn(n, EZXML_WS)) = ';';` with insufficient bounds checking on the DTD token region.

Out-of-bounds read while parsing a crafted XML file: after a strcspn scan reaches the end of the buffer, subsequent dereferences read past the input. Some secondary sources attribute this CVE to ezxml_internal_dtd; the OSV/SourceForge primary record names ezxml_parse_str, used here so it does not collide with V1.

validation.method: Fix commit 7e4c59b6 ('htmlescape: fix off-by-one and overflow', 2020-01-10) is the same-day descendant of this commit; the pre-fix htmlescape here under-allocates and mis-terminates the escape buffer.
validation.poc_source: public: LibreDWG issue #182 ('Several bugs found by fuzzing')

vulnerabilities.sink_description: htmlescape() allocates `malloc(strlen(src)+10)` (escape.c:35, uninitialized) then strcat()s multi-byte HTML entity replacements (e.g. """ = 6 bytes, escape.c:49-56) while advancing with an off-by-one `while(*s++)` loop (escape.c:38) and a too-loose `off >= len-8` guard, so a text value with many escapable characters overruns the heap buffer. Reached from output_TEXT() at dwg2SVG.c:135 / :400. The CVE text cites escape.c:46/48/51, which are line numbers from the 0.10.2641 build, not this commit.

evidence.asan_summary: heap-buffer-overflow in htmlescape via strcat, programs/escape.c:46/48/51, called from output_TEXT (programs/dwg2SVG.c)
evidence.note: CVE-2020-21816/21818/21819 are the same htmlescape heap overflow pinned to escape.c lines 46/48/51; Veritas records a single ground-truth OOB for this commit. Aliases: htmlwescape has the same bug (fixed in e8c3edb), output_TEXT is the caller.

validation.method: 93c2512 is an ancestor of the commit tested in issue #615 (3c90dc66) and predates the fix ae09b9b7 ('decode: fail on wrong r2000 Classes header', 2023-01-30).
validation.needs_confirmation: dwg2dxf reaches several heap OOBs in the DWG decode path. CVE-2023-25222 (bit_read_RC) is the best dwg2dxf-specific public match. If the Veritas artifact names a different sink for this commit, update this entry (see `alternatives`).

vulnerabilities.cwe_note: NVD lists CWE-787; the public ASan report shows a 1-byte READ, so CWE-125 is used here.
vulnerabilities.sink_description: While decoding the AcDb:Classes section of a crafted DWG, an invalid section size lets the reader run past the end of the heap-allocated file buffer. ASan (at the reported commit): 1-byte READ one byte left of a 652-byte region in bit_read_RC (src/bits.c:320), reached via bit_read_RS -> bit_read_RL -> decode_R13_R2000 (src/decode.c:682).
fix_commits: ae09b9b7b51bda4a719279a6ade6dadeaf5ef39f (decode: fail on wrong r2000 Classes header, Fixes GH #615)

alternatives.note: heap-buffer-overflow in bit_utf8_to_TU (GH #681), reproduced via dwg2SVG rather than dwg2dxf, so a weaker match for this binary. Fix c1ed1d91.

validation.method: Fix commit 1b71a6ba ('fix heap-buffer-overflow in mp4read.c', 2020-08-31) is a descendant of this commit; at 1073aee the stszin() integer-overflow allocation is still present. (1073aee itself fixes a different stack overflow in stringin()/ftypin(), issue #56.)

vulnerabilities.sink_description: stszin() reads the stsz entry count into mp4config.frame.ents (a u32). `malloc(sizeof(*data) * (ents + 1))` overflows to malloc(0) when ents == 0xFFFFFFFF, and the subsequent `mp4config.frame.data[0] = ofs;` plus the per-entry loop write past the zero-size allocation.
trigger_path: integer overflow at malloc (mp4read.c:348); OOB write at mp4read.c:355

evidence.asan_summary: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 at stszin mp4read.c:355, region alloc'd at mp4read.c:348
